text:
maya: i'm taking over nightpass, quick summary of what to watch — embedding pipelines still noisy, customer-facing regen errors from EU, and a minor routing fallback in us-west. details below.

incident-bot: ALERT triggered: embeddings-queue.p99_latency > 800ms (svc: embeddings-queue, region: eu-west)
pagerduty-bot: Pager duty alert created (INC-2026-ALPHA) — assigned to maya

maya: active items —
- embeddings-queue p99 latency spike (eu-west). suspected cache evictions during heavy batches. dashboards: https://redwood.monitoring/embeddings/queue?range=1h
- customer "Fjord Labs" seeing intermittent 502s on regenerate calls in eu-west (affects ~8% of requests last 10m)
- routing fallback: us-west requests temporarily routed to cp-secondary (higher latency but healthy) — autoswitch configured to revert after 15m if stable

sasha: thanks. are there any ongoing mitigation steps in progress?

maya: yes —
- scaled embeddings-workers +2 in eu-west (manual, will hold for 20m to see effect)
- increased cache TTL for prefix-cache (temporary) via config rollout: `curl -XPOST https://config.internal/api/v1/rollouts -d '{"key":"prefix_cache.ttl","value":60}'`
- for Fjord Labs, added a per-customer retry header to reduce 502s, and enabled read-fallback to cached outputs where available

eli: i've got the prim/secondary warmup script running for eu-west, keeping an eye on kv-eviction metrics. sharing the query i used to spot the eviction spike:```sql
SELECT minute, evictions FROM kv_stats WHERE region='eu-west' AND minute > now() - interval '30 minutes' ORDER BY minute DESC LIMIT 30;
```

noah: note — logs show a burst of large requests from a single client ip that correlates with the eviction spike. i've throttled that IP at the load-balancer (temp).

maya: action items for whoever takes over: 
1) primary for next hour: tariq (please watch p99s and redirect if needed)
2) secondary: eli (observe kv metrics; ready to swap to secondary if prim degrades)
3) if embeddings p99 stays > 700ms for > 15m, trigger gradual rollback of the prefix-cache TTL change and re-evaluate batching windows.
4) for any customer 5xx > 5% in 10m escalate to customer-ops and add incident label `customer-impact`.

tariq: ack — i'll be primary. quick Q: where's the runbook for embeddings-queue?

maya: runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/runbooks/embeddings-queue ; short checklist in there under "eviction spike". also see ops-playbook -> batching isolation.

tariq: got it. i'll keep the scaling step available. if p95 > 400ms for > 10m i'll flip traffic to eu-north recovery pool and notify sales if customers affected. :thumbsup:

eli: reminder — if you need to collect a heapdump from a worker: `kubectl exec -c runtime-worker <pod> -- /usr/local/bin/collect-heap.sh` then upload to /var/tmp/ops-dumps and ping eng-runtime.

sasha: thanks team. any estimated ETA for stabilization?

maya: early expectation: scaling + TTL should show improvements in 10-15m. if not, we'll fallback to routing change. i'm leaving notes in the incident doc: https://incident.redwood/INC-2026-ALPHA

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-ALPHA state changed -> acknowledged by maya

noah: added a watch on customer traffic spikes and set an alert for >3 distinct customers with regen errors in 15m window.

tariq: i'm taking over now. primary contact: @tariq. i'll post a 30m check-in. filing a short checklist: `scale workers -> monitor p99 -> revert ttl if no improvement -> escalate to runtime`

eli: secondary standby. i'll be available for swap or to run the heapdump command.

maya: thanks, leaving the channel. tag me if you need escalation (i'll be reachable via PD). good handoff. :wave:
